track_pick.18: Spin Spin Sugar (Armand's Dark Garage Mix)

video_note.10: featured cut = the Underground Goodie mix — the squelchy B-side, not the piano-led Original
video_note.18: featured cut = Armand's Dark Garage Mix — the wobbling low-end blueprint for speed garage

row_note.1: Italo squelch before house: a rubbery analogue bassline (Roland MC-202, not a 303) that Chicago and Detroit DJs adored — the disco end of the thread.
row_note.2: The 303 played as a bass guitar — Chicago jack with a soulful hook; the squelch enters the club lineage.
row_note.3: Jamie Principle's gospel-carnal vocal over a snaking analogue bassline — proto-acid soul from the Godfather's camp.
row_note.4: Diva vocal over a resonant analogue bassline — the Hot Mix 5 blueprint for squelch under soul.
row_note.5: Vocal acid house that crossed over — Maurice Joshua crooning the craze itself, soul voice on a 303 floor.
row_note.6: DJ Pierre's deep-acid beauty — strings over squelch, acid house at its most soulful.
row_note.7: London proto-garage: deep squelching bass under a UK soul vocal, years before 'UK garage' meant anything.
row_note.8: The squelchiest bassline ever to grace the pop charts — Chicago house sensuality, disco at heart.
row_note.9: DJ Pierre's Wild Pitch on Strictly Rhythm — filtered squelch rising for ten minutes under Paula Brion's vocal.
row_note.10: Gospel-house anthem from Cajmere's Chicago — the Underground Goodie mix rides a rubber-squelch bassline.
row_note.11: 🎧 Junior Boy's Own garage with an acid undertow — UK house facing New York; ear-check the acid credential.
row_note.12: Strictly Rhythm acid-stab anthem — the 303-style riff IS the hook; the Dark Ages Mix is the original 12"'s A-side.
row_note.13: G-funk squelch from the filter-house cornerstone — first released on Soma in 1995; this master anchors the Virgin pressing.
row_note.14: Armand's NY garage remix whose warping bassline wrote the speed garage blueprint — warp, not strictly 303, and canonical for it.
row_note.15: Basement Jaxx's breakout — garage swing with an acid line snaking through the brass.
row_note.16: THE speed garage detonation — its warping bass is acid squelch's jungle-pressured descendant.
row_note.17: Speed garage at its most acidic — the bassline bends like an overdriven 303 under the ragga chat.
row_note.19: Squelchy speed garage bump from the Jeremy Sylvester / Nice 'n' Ripe camp — known by its vocal hook 'what you want, what you need'.
row_note.20: Literal acid garage — a 303 flexed over a 137bpm UKG skip; the thread made explicit at UKG's peak.
row_note.21: A UKG dubplate legend on Resurrection — the warping, acid-adjacent bassline every revivalist still chases.
row_note.22: Disco-punk-house squelch — analogue filth from the Emperor Machine camp; the disco end, twenty years on.
row_note.23: DFA's 303 meltdown — nine minutes of disco-punk building to a full acid boil.
row_note.24: Space disco: arpeggiated analogue squelch as melody — Norway extending the disco thread.
row_note.25: Kerri Chandler's resonant stab-riff — deep house royalty flirting with squelch; NJ lineage.
row_note.26: Filter-house lineage with a wobbling resonant bass — the record that seeded fidget house.
row_note.27: Bassline's crossover moment — Sheffield's Niche sound, warped bass under a northern soul voice.
row_note.28: DJ Q's Niche-era classic — bassline house at full strut before the scene was policed away.
row_note.29: The warping-bass house record of 2012 — Bristol garage swing, pure rubber.
row_note.30: Nu-disco's squelchiest earworm — press coverage called out its 'gloriously fat acid 303s'.
row_note.31: The 2012 garage-house revival's acid moment — squelch riding a shuffling UKG-house beat.
row_note.32: A chart-crossing jack track — squelchy loop bass on the house/garage borderline.
row_note.33: Lobster Theremin's very first record — arpeggio squelch over dreamy deep house.
row_note.34: 'We Make Acid': 303 + 707 with Paris Brightledge's Chicago-soul vocal — acid house proper with a soulful heart, the brief's spirit incarnate.
row_note.36: Glasgow euphoria — a resonant rubber bassline carrying the whole emotional load.
row_note.37: Italo-disco arp squelch on Running Back — Neutron Dance lives on The Division EP.
row_note.38: Rufus & Chaka Khan reborn over squelchy resonant stabs — the lockdown-era Scottish anthem.
row_note.39: Bumping garage-house with a proper acid line — the DJOKO alias at its squelchiest.
row_note.40: Acid-soaked disco-pop built for the floor — the vinyl 12" adds an Extended UKG Mix that ties it back to the garage thread.
row_note.41: It says what it does: NYC bassline-house jack with a Squelch-A-Pella on the flip.
row_note.42: The decade's big-room garage-techno moment — a wriggling rubber bassline heard in every rave since.
